refill_credit_comparison.note: REPORT ONLY: total triangular-kernel credit over the pinned H19-5 proxy support. A larger marginal credit means the refill covers more currently-uncredited support pixels; it is not a score and does not rank a file.

mechanism_card.hypothesis: The recorded A4/L2 collar deletes 2,632 near-catalogue R0 dots and then restores the same count with the lineage's FIFO-BFS traversal order, which places 98.7-99.5 % of replacements within 3 px of a dot already retained. That ordering is a tie-break, not the metric: it adds the 0.2*(S-M) penalty while supplying almost no fresh kernel credit. Replacing it with the metric's own marginal kernel credit -- evaluated truth-free on the same H19-5 proxy support -- should put each replacement where it covers currently-uncredited corroborated-ridge pixels, i.e. the pixels the collar deletion orphaned, and therefore recover more coverage per replacement.
mechanism_card.mechanism: Ellipse (along/2)^2 + (across/4)^2 <= 1 removes the collar dots; the exact 37654 dot count is restored from outside-collar H19-5 support (d_cat>2 px, the parent baseline) by a greedy max-marginal-credit rule with exact local credit updates inside the 300 m kernel. Marginal credit of a candidate q is sum_offsets max(0, k*support[q+off] - credit[q+off]) + own-pixel term, with credit the current best kernel credit from dots already placed. Ties break on flat raster index, so the file is byte-reproducible. Catalogue pixels remain exactly zero mass.
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: The orphaned pixels the credit-aware refill targets are adjacent to mapped traces, where lithologic contacts, drainage divides and shoreline/road alignments mimic faults; a refill that concentrates mass there can simply re-add the false mass the collar removed. H19-5 is also the parent's own support, so 'covering H19-5 pixels' is not the same as covering undisclosed truth, and the H19-5 field itself fires on the known catalogue.
mechanism_card.predicted_live_change: +0.004 DTI (MODEL; plausible -0.008 to +0.012; not a score)
mechanism_card.prediction_decomposition: MODEL: the collar term is unchanged from the recorded FIFO twin (same collar, same pool, same count); only the refill term changes. On the H19-5 proxy the credit-aware refill supplies 4054 kernel credit versus 1215 for the FIFO ordering (difference +2840), so the prediction is the recorded twin's collar gain plus a refill term proportional to that difference, discounted because proxy-support credit is not truth credit.
mechanism_card.falsifier: A paired same-week live receipt against the recorded FIFO twin (h33-h33-2-b2-PRUNEanisoA4L2-20261023-0bf248e2) with delta <= -0.010 rejects the refill-ordering mechanism at this collar width; |delta| < 0.010 is no evidence. A monotone decline across A4->A6 would also falsify the mechanism, since the credit-aware refill's advantage should persist while the collar widens.
mechanism_card.structural_geologist_note: Inspect where the credit-aware refill placed mass relative to the retained strands: the prediction is that it fills the gaps the collar deletion opened beside mapped traces, not that it invents new structures. If the replacements simply re-occupy the deleted flank positions, the collar and the refill are cancelling and the edit is a no-op.
